knowledge_point.title: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using Gaussian Elimination

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=8 \\ 4x-7y &=14.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 8 \\ 4 & -7 & 14\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 8 \\ 4 & -7 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 4 & -7 & 14\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=4 \\ y &=-2,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-2$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-2)=4\,⇒\,x=0.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=-2.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x-4y &=4 \\ 4x-7y &=7.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & -7 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & -4 & 4 \\ 4 & -7 & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 4 & -7 & 7\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$

The system is now 

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y &=2 \\ y &=-1,\end{aligned}\right.
$$

and we can apply back substitution. The final equation $y=-1$ tells us the value of $y.$ Substituting this value into the first equation, we get

$$
x-2(-1)=2\,⇒\,x=0.
$$

Thus, the solution is $x=0$ and $y=-1.$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}2x+7y &=-32 \\ 7x+11y &=-58.\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 7 & -32 \\ 7 & 11 & -58\end{array}\right].
$$

Reducing $M$ to row echelon form, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 7 & -32 \\ 7 & 11 & -58\end{array}\right] & {R}_{1} & :=\frac{1}{2}{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -16 \\ 7 & 11 & -58\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-7{R}_{1} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -16 \\ 0 & -\frac{27}{2} & 54\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{2}{27}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & \frac{7}{2} & -16 \\ 0 & 1 & -4\end{array}\right].\end{aligned}
$$
